chunks.heading: Land cover training data > Land cover per lot
chunks.text:
- Allentown and the first towns of the three older county places (Chester, Centre, Montgomery): only Centre County lies in a Chesapeake test county (about 0.70 test mIoU there, with Cumberland). Allentown, Chester and Montgomery are not validated: no labeled land cover there. Each record says so in `quality.assumptions`. The hard surface counts toward an impervious cap where a town file sets one. Since the Nov 15 rebuild their `spot_cover` is filled from the same model's class maps (`processed/<place>/cover_work/r34_c5_s0/tiles/`, read by `pipeline/vision/cover_lookup.py`). So the spot figures have the same accuracy as the lot shares. 36 College Township lots have no cover row. The towns added to Chester, Montgomery and Centre County on 2026-11-27 and 28 have no cover row. Their `spot_cover` reads the same class maps (the tile folders were last written 2026-11-15), so it is filled only where those maps reach (West Goshen lots carry it, checked 2026-11-28). The nine new places have no class maps, so no `spot_cover`. The assistant's lot tools give the accuracy note with the tree and paving shares, and with the figures inside the suggested spot.

Known limits:

- Labels are 1 m and are put on the 0.6 m image grid, so class edges are uncertain by about one pixel.
- There are no Chesapeake labels for western Pennsylvania. The Pittsburgh raster covers only part of the city.
- The city rasters are older than the photos the model sees (2017 and 2019 against 2022). Lots that changed since show up as disagreement.

chunks.heading: Places: where can you build an ADU today, for every Pennsylvania municipality
chunks.text:
Not legal advice. Not a zoning determination.

ADU rules in Pennsylvania are set town by town, not by the state. This table gives every county subdivision
(2,572 rows: the 2,560 municipalities, with the 12 that cross a county line split into their parts) one best answer,
says how good the evidence is, and names the source and its date.

- Data file for the app and the assistant: `app/public/data/pa_places.json` (one object per place) and
  `app/public/data/pa_places_meta.json` (sources, counts, conflicts).
- Builder: `python -m pipeline.places_index build`. Analysis: `python -m pipeline.places_index analyze`.
- Fuller table on the data drive: `<data root>/processed/places/pa_places.csv` and `pa_places_conflicts.csv`.
- Raw downloads and their licences: `<data root>/raw/places/` with `SOURCES.json`.
- Contract (field names, enums, examples): top of `<data root>/ops/logs/pa-places.md`.

chunks.heading: The answer ladder
chunks.text:
Every place gets exactly one tier, the best evidence found for it:

| Tier | What it means | Where the status comes from |
|---|---|---|
| `verified` | Hand-read rule file, checked a second time | `shared/rules`, index status verified |
| `drafted` | Hand-read rule file with open points | index status drafted. The open point is in `status_detail` |
| `reported` | A dated planning-agency inventory, or the state's record that the place has no zoning | inventory row, or DCED Municipal Statistics |
| `text_search` | The town's public zoning text can be searched for quotes. No status is claimed | tier B corpus |
| `baseline` | Nothing local is known. The statewide baseline applies | `shared/rules/pa_statewide.json` |

And exactly one status:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `by_right` | A zoning permit when the standards are met |
| `limited` | Allowed with a limit: family only, a hearing (special exception or conditional use), conversion only, only in some districts, or an owner-occupancy rule. `status_detail` says which. `approval` tells a permit path (`by_right`) apart from a hearing |
| `not_addressed` | The code has no ADU use. A use variance at best |
| `prohibited` | The code bars ADUs |
| `no_zoning` | The municipality has no zoning ordinance and no county ordinance applies. Zoning does not limit an ADU. The building code (UCC), sewage permits (Act 537), deeds and HOA rules still apply |
| `unknown` | Not known. Allowed only at `text_search` and `baseline` |

Rules that keep it honest:

chunks.heading: The answer ladder
chunks.text:
- A rule file always wins. Where an inventory or the DCED record disagrees with a rule file, the place keeps the rule
  file answer and the disagreement goes to the conflicts list for a reviewer.
- A reported status is never promoted to verified.
- Nothing is inferred from neighbours, from county averages or from machine-read drafts.
- Every status has a source with a date. An old inventory keeps its year in `source.date`.
- Status mapping from rule files: `allowed_by_right` to `by_right` (or `limited` with an owner-occupancy rule or a
  district scope); `special_exception`, `conditional_use`, `family_only`, `conversion_only` to `limited`;
  `not_addressed`, `prohibited` as is. Unit types: `detached_new` to `detached`, `garage_conversion` and `over_garage`
  to `garage`, `internal` and `attached` as is.

chunks.heading: Who zones: zoning_authority
chunks.text:
Source: Pennsylvania DCED, Municipal Statistics, report "Municipal/County Planning, Zoning & Building Codes"
(apps.dced.pa.gov/Munstats-public, report CountyMuniBuilding_Excel), exported for all counties on 2026-11-12. The
fields come from the land use section of the annual DCED-CLGS-19 report each municipality files. The site says the data
are refreshed nightly. The filing year of each municipality is not shown.

| Value | Rule |
|---|---|
| `municipal` | The municipality files a zoning ordinance (its own or a joint one) |
| `county` | No own ordinance, the county files a county zoning ordinance, the municipality says county zoning applies, and the county's own list names it (when it gives one). Also every place a county web page lists under its ordinance (Luzerne, as of 2026-04-22; Lycoming Zoning Partnership) |
| `none` | No own ordinance, no county zoning, and no county list names it |
| `unknown` | The records disagree. Most often a municipality says county zoning applies in a county that files no county ordinance |

A municipality split across counties has a DCED row in each. A YES in any row counts for all its parts (Telford, McDonald,
Ellwood City, Tunnelhill and Falls Creek have a stub row that says NO).

Check against independent research: the corpus availability survey (`<data root>/corpus/availability.csv`, web research on
2026-11-11) had a zoning answer for 116 places. DCED agrees on 115: all 105 municipal, the 1 joint ordinance, all 4 with
no zoning and 5 of 6 county places (the sixth is `unknown` here).

chunks.heading: Contacts
chunks.text:
From DCED Municipal Statistics, "County / Municipal Contact Person": the phone and website each municipality filed.
`contact.office` is a generic label (`Township office`). DCED names no zoning office, so the assistant should say "ask the
township office for the zoning officer". Names, emails and street addresses are not copied (some small townships file
a secretary's home address). 2,570 places have a phone, 1,497 a website.

chunks.heading: Zoning code link
chunks.text:
`code_url` links to the place's zoning code: the `code_url` of its `shared/rules/towns_index.json` entry (every entry,
towns not yet read included, and the other part of a split municipality), else the rule file's provenance link. `null`
for every other place; the app then shows the town website from `contact.url`, or no link.

chunks.heading: Population and homes
chunks.text:
`pop` is the Census Vintage 2025 subcounty estimate (July 1, 2025), the file the MUSA 5500 `get_data.py` reads (https://github.com/yezhanggg/YZMUSA5500).
Mount Lebanon and Penn Hills are found under their new codes by name. Wheatland borough (Mercer) has no 2025 estimate
and keeps its 2020 count. `housing_units` is the 2020 Census (PL 94-171 HU100), the file `tools/town_targets.py` reads.

chunks.heading: Inventories
chunks.text:
Open, dated, municipality-by-municipality ADU inventories for Pennsylvania are scarce. A search of county and regional
planning agencies, the state, university and nonprofit trackers (2026-11-12, about 50 searches, robots.txt obeyed, no
code hosts) found one full county inventory and a handful of examples. Rows are transcribed, never inferred
(`raw/places/inventories/inventory_rows.csv`, 95 rows; sources and terms in `SOURCES_inventories.json`).

| id | Publisher, title | Date | Places used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ycpc_senior_housing_2024` | York County Planning Commission, Senior Housing Opportunities by Municipality (ADU column by district) | 2024-09 (PDF date, no data date given) | 34 with a status, 2 no zoning |
| `chesco_missingmiddle_2023` | Chester County Planning Commission, Missing Middle guide, ADU examples | about 2023-01 | 4 |
| `centre_housing_needs_2005` | Centre County Affordable Housing Needs Assessment, Table 28 | 2005 | 3 (2 more not used, see conflicts) |
| `dvrpc_mit_toolbox_2019` | DVRPC Municipal Implementation Toolbox, Plumstead case | 2019 | 1 |
| `berkeley_zrt_2026` | UC Berkeley Othering & Belonging Institute, Zoning Reform Tracker | 2026-02-28 | 1 (East Lampeter), plus a cross-check on Philadelphia |

How rows are used:

chunks.heading: Inventories
chunks.text:
- Only a dated row with a status sets a status. The newest dated inventory wins. Its date is in `source.date` and at the
  end of `status_detail` ("inventory dated 2005").
- A row with no status, or with no date (the Chester County eTools pages), is added to `status_detail` as an
  "Inventory note, no status claimed" beside `unknown`. 35 places carry such a note (most are York County places where
  the table lists no ADU-type use; the table lists only permitted uses, so silence is not read as "not addressed").
- The York table says "No Zoning" for Wellsville and York Haven boroughs, where the DCED records disagree (no own ordinance,
  county zoning claimed in a county with none). The two agree on no own ordinance, so these two are `no_zoning` with the
  York County source.
- An inventory that itself says the place had no zoning code (Centre 2005: Worth and Rush townships, "permitted" and
  "no local zoning code") is not used where DCED now records zoning.
- The DCED record (2026) is newer than every inventory. Where it says no zoning, it wins over an older inventory.

Checked and not usable: Lancaster County 2009 regulatory barriers study (municipalities not named), Cumberland County
2023 review and 2024 plan, Tri-County RPC fact sheet, DVRPC 2007 tool and Housing Snapshots, Montgomery County "Promoting
Workforce Housing" (404 after a site move, three tries), National Zoning Atlas (PA county data sold under licence through
Land Use Labs, map site robots.txt blocks bots), Urban Institute land-use survey (bot check, no workaround), Pew 2025,
PA Housing Action Plan 2026, Housing Alliance of PA, PlanningPA, and no inventory found for LVPC, Bucks, Delaware, Berks,
Allegheny, SPC, Erie, Westmoreland, Beaver, Washington, Butler or Lebanon.

chunks.heading: File size
chunks.text:
1.44 MB raw, about 105 KB gzipped. The contract keeps full key names, and with 2,572 rows the names alone weigh about
650 KB, so the 700 KB raw target cannot be met with them. Short keys would give about 0.95 MB. Static hosts send JSON
gzipped.

chunks.heading: What the assistant should say
chunks.text:
- `verified` or `drafted`: answer from the rule file (`get_rule_text`), as today. Drafted: say the open point.
- `reported` with an inventory: "<publisher> reported in <year> that ...". Say it is a planning-agency summary, not the
  code, and may be out of date.
- `no_zoning`: "<Place> has no zoning ordinance on file with the state (DCED, 2026), so zoning does not limit an ADU.
  You still need a building permit and a sewage permit." House Bill 2186 would not change this.
- `text_search`: search the text and quote it. No conclusion without a quote.
- `baseline`: the statewide baseline, and "this town's code is not in my data". Give the contact.
- Always end with: ask the zoning officer before you design or build.

chunks.heading: Tracts
chunks.text:
Zoning is set by each town, and a census tract can cross a town line. `python -m pipeline.tract.towns` splits every
tract's homes and people between towns from the 2020 Census blocks (`tl_2020_42_tabblock20`) and the Census block
assignment file, which places every block in one county subdivision. No shapes are overlaid, so the split is exact:
every town's home count matches the 2020 count.

- 674 of 3,445 tracts cross a town line. They hold 21.3% of the state's homes.
- In 266 tracts the towns that hold at least 1% of the homes have different statuses.
- Files: `<data root>/processed/tract_town_xwalk.csv` (all pairs) and `app/public/data/tract_towns.json` (pairs with
  at least 0.5% of the tract's homes or people).
- The tool's tract answer stays the answer of the town where the map was clicked. The Allowed row adds the split
  when a tract crosses a town line. The assistant's `get_area_stats` on a tract lists every town with its share of
  homes and its rule today.

chunks.heading: Architecture
chunks.text:
This product answers one question for a home lot in Pennsylvania: can a backyard home (an ADU) go here, how big, under which rules, and does it pay. 14 lot places are covered lot by lot (lot data 13, Nov 28, 2026): Philadelphia (459,998 lots), Pittsburgh (92,081), Allentown (29,158), Erie (26,150), and towns in Montgomery (142,072), Delaware (104,738), Lancaster (62,735), Bucks (48,764), Chester (42,306), York (40,295), Dauphin (35,475), Northampton (33,695), Cumberland (10,259) and Centre (6,827) counties, 1,134,553 lots in all. 223 towns beyond the two cities have a hand-read rule file (98 of them are in the lot places), as of Nov 27, 2026: with the two cities, 201 verified and 24 drafted. Every Pennsylvania place gets one answer from the answer ladder, down to a statewide baseline. Towns outside the lot places have rules but no lot files.

Not legal advice. Not a zoning determination. Parcel lines are not a survey.

chunks.heading: Three steps for the user
chunks.text:
| Step | What the user does | What answers it |
|---|---|---|
| Find | Search an address or pan the map. Pick a lot. | The lot index and the per-tract lot files (`lots/<place>/index.parquet`, `app/<GEOID>.json`, `detail/<GEOID>.json.gz`) |
| Test | Draw or size a unit. See if it fits, under which scenario, and why not. | The saved lot record (rules, buildable ground, fit per ADU type), checked again in the browser by `app/src/lib/lot/verdict.ts` and `app/src/lib/fitBox.ts` |
| Build | Read the steps from rules to rental license, with fees and the money picture. | `app/src/lib/lot/buildSteps.ts` and the money model (`pipeline/money.py`, `app/src/lib/money.ts`) |

The browser library for these steps is in `app/src/lib/lot/`. The Testing mode of the tool uses it (`app/src/tool/test/`), and so do the assistant's lot tools. See [app/src/lib/lot/README.md](../app/src/lib/lot/README.md).

```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Sources A[City and county layers
parcels, footprints, zoning,
overlays, flood, slope, streets] B[Assessor tables
OPA, Allegheny assessments] C[OSM service roads
Microsoft footprints] D[Census TIGER tracts] E[HUD SAFMR rents] G[City land cover rasters
NAIP 2022 model cover] end subgraph Place tables P[processed/place/
lots, buildings, streets, alleys] end subgraph Rules and fit R[shared/rules/*.json
pipeline/rules.py] F[pipeline/fit.py] end subgraph Lot files L[lots/place/
detail, index, app, manifest] end APP[app/src/lib/lot
Find, Test, Build] A --> P B --> P C --> P P --> L D --> L E --> L R --> L F --> L G --> L L --> APP M[shared/assumptions.json
pipeline/money.py, money.ts] --> APP ``` In words:

chunks.heading: Data flow
chunks.text:
1. Each place module downloads its layers once into `raw/<place>/` and records each one in `raw/<place>/SOURCES.json`.
2. The place `build` step joins parcels, assessor rows, zoning, overlays, flags and building outlines into one lots table and one buildings table per place, in `processed/<place>/`.
3. The lot builder (`pipeline/build_lots.py`) reads those tables. For every lot and each of the three scenarios (today, local reform, state reform) it resolves the rules (`pipeline/rules.py`), finds the front, rear and side lot lines, cuts the buildable ground and fits each allowed ADU type (`pipeline/fit.py`). The fit is a vector geometry test on lot, building and street lines with rule-based setbacks.
4. It joins land cover per lot and, in the places of lot data 12, reads what lies inside the suggested spot (trees a unit would remove, open ground, hard surface). Land cover is context. It does not move or block the unit.
   A later refresh step (`build_lots terrain`) adds ground slope from the USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM: over the lot, the buildable ground and under the suggested spot, a steep flag and a second fit on ground under 25 percent. Slope is context too. It does not change the fit's yes or no.
5. It writes one validated JSON record per lot, grouped by 2020 census tract, plus a compact index, the current app's per-tract lists and a manifest.
6. The browser loads a tract file, shows the saved answer, and tests a unit the user draws against the saved buildable ground.

Land cover and the detector, by place:

chunks.heading: Data flow
chunks.text:
| | Philadelphia | Pittsburgh | Allentown and the first 9 county-place towns (lot data 12). The lots added on Nov 27 and 28 have an empty cover block (as of 2026-11-28) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lot `cover` block | The city's 2018 land cover raster (`landcover_2018`), because the model is not reliable for tree and open ground on NAIP 2022 here | The three-model land cover ensemble on NAIP 2022 (`model:div7_3m_tta`), from `cover_model_div7_3m_tta.parquet`, since 2026-11-18. Before that `r34_c5_s0` | The same model, from `cover.parquet` (Nov 14). Validated only in Centre County (a Chesapeake test county). 36 Centre County lots have none |
| Cover inside the suggested spot (`spot_cover`) | From the same raster | From the same model maps | From the same model maps (since the Nov 15 rebuild) |
| Detector objects | Not in the lot records (`objects` is empty) | Not in the lot records (`objects` is empty) | Not in the lot records |

- The land cover model (`pipeline/vision/`) scores aerial images as building, tree, open ground, hard surface and other. See [MODEL_CARD_landcover.md](MODEL_CARD_landcover.md).
- The object detector (`musa6950/yolo/`) finds garages, sheds, other accessory buildings and pools in sample areas only. It writes `processed/yolo/detections_<city>.parquet`. Its labels are first pass and its scores are not a true accuracy, so it does not feed the lot records. Garages and sheds in the fit come from building outlines.

chunks.heading: Three tiers of zoning knowledge
chunks.text:
Not legal advice. Not a zoning determination. Parcel lines are not a survey.

| Tier | Where | What it holds | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Lot-level rules | The 14 lot places (`shared/rules/philadelphia.json`, `pittsburgh.json`, the town files of Allentown and the 97 county-place towns, plus the bill files) | Every rule resolved for every lot and scenario, with district setbacks and overlays, saved in the lot record | Lot files, Testing mode, the assistant's lot tools |
| 2. Town rule files | 223 towns beyond the two cities, mostly the largest by 2020 population (`shared/rules/pa_<county>_<town>.json`). With the two cities, 201 verified and 24 drafted with a stated open point (2026-11-27) | ADU status, approval path, size, owner occupancy, conditions and other ways to add a unit, each cited. Lot files only for the towns in the lot places | The assistant (`get_rule_text`, `list_rule_places`), `pipeline/rules.py` town resolver, [RULES_TOWNS.md](RULES_TOWNS.md) |
| 2b. Public zoning text (unverified) | 66 towns with a public copy of the ordinance on the town or a county site (`<data root>/corpus/tierb/`, published as `zoning_text/` next to the lot data) | Passages copied word for word, with section, pages, link and fetch date. No verdict | The assistant (`search_zoning_text`, `list_text_places`), only for a town with no rule file or a detail the rule file lacks. Labelled "unverified text search" |

chunks.heading: Three tiers of zoning knowledge
chunks.text:
| 3. Statewide baseline | Every other Pennsylvania town (`shared/rules/pa_statewide.json`) | MPC approval paths, building code, sewage rules, the pending bills. No town zoning numbers | The assistant, which says the answer is the statewide baseline and not the town's own code |

Tier 2b is built by `pipeline/corpus/tierb.py` from the machine-read pilot (`pipeline/corpus/`). The pilot's machine drafts (status, path, districts) stay out of the product. See [CORPUS.md](CORPUS.md).

chunks.heading: How the assistant answers
chunks.text:
For any question about what a Pennsylvania municipality allows, the assistant calls `get_place_answer` first
(`app/src/agent/placeAnswer.ts`). For one lot in a place with lot records (Pittsburgh, Philadelphia, Allentown, Chester County, Centre County, Montgomery County: the
list comes from `PLACE_BY_COUNTY` in `app/src/lib/lot/load.ts` through `app/src/agent/lotPlaces.ts`, so the wording
needs no change for a new city) the lot tools come first. The tool
resolves the place (name, "name, county", GEOID, or the town selected on the map; a shared name such as the 22
Washington townships gets a question back, never a guess), reads its row in `app/public/data/pa_places.json` and
walks the ladder. The assistant never answers "I don't know": it gives the best grounded answer with its label and the
next step, and never invents a rule, a section or a number.

chunks.heading: How the assistant answers
chunks.text:
| Tier | Where from | What the answer says | Confidence label |
|---|---|---|---|
| verified | Hand-checked rule file | The rule as fact: forms, size cap, approval, conditions, sections | "Checked rule file, verified on <date>" |
| drafted | Rule file with open points | The answer, plus the open points | "First reading of the town's code (<date>), with open points" |
| reported | Dated public record (DCED Municipal Statistics: no zoning ordinance) | "Allowed, no zoning here": building code, sewage permits, deeds still apply | "<publisher> (<year>) lists ... Not checked against the code here" |
| text_search | Public zoning text (tier 2b) | Quoted passages, no verdict, plus the statewide baseline | "Unverified text search" |
| baseline | `shared/rules/pa_statewide.json` | Who zones here (own, county or none), the MPC paths, the bills (not law), who to ask and the question to ask | "Statewide baseline, not this town's code" |

With a unit type or size, the tool also checks the proposal against the rule file (form allowed, size cap) and says
why it fits or not. The answer format (verdict line, "Zoning here allows", "Your proposal", "Why it does or does not
fit", source and confidence, "Next step") is in the system prompt (`agent/schema.ts`). Eval: `agent/eval/questions_ladder.json`.

What the tool results carry so the model does not have to infer it (the prompt stays short):

chunks.heading: How the assistant answers
chunks.text:
- Rule text from the resolver: a status per form (`adu.status_by_form`, `approval.by_form_today`) gives a "Depends on
  the form" verdict with one line per form; a lesser-of cap comes as one sentence (`size_rule_*`, "At most 1,000 sq ft
  or 50% of the house, whichever is less"); `who_decides` names the body that hears a special exception (Zoning
  Hearing Board) or conditional use (governing body), per form; a `code_caution` line (placeholder code, amendments not
  seen) comes first; an ADU under another listing is named as such. A proposal check says the share-of-house cap is
  "Not checked" when the house size is not known.
- Text search: every passage sits in a `quote` field, with a `quote_rule` line (copy character for character, cut with
  "..." around stray marks, never fix a word) and `text_kind` ("scanned text, quoted as read" for OCR). In scanned
  text a misread word stays misread inside the quotes (`SCANNED_NOTE`). To fix it, the answer says that piece in its own
  words outside the quotes. A search with
  no match returns `say_exactly: "Not found in the text searched."` and a `not_found_rule`.
- Lot records: a check the record cannot test (no house size, no land cover block) has `pass: "not checked"`, and
  `test_unit_on_lot` lists them under `not_checked`. A record with land cover gives a `land_cover` block in
  `get_lot_facts` (and in `test_unit_on_lot` for a backyard cottage): tree, paving, open ground and building shares of
  the whole lot, the record's accuracy note from `quality.assumptions`, and the trees and paving inside the suggested

chunks.heading: How the assistant answers
chunks.text:
spot, or a line saying they are not available for the place. A `rule` line says to give the accuracy note with the
  figures.
- Address search: `find_lot` reads a static address index per place (`<place>/addresses/`, 3.6 MB for the six
  places of lot data 12, in the lot data bundle; Delaware County lots have no address, see [DATA.md](DATA.md#address-index)). It finds any address in a lot place, on the
  map or not. It works on the live site only once the bundle is published.

Questions about the tool itself (how it works, data sources, accuracy, limits, coverage, figures, what changed when,
hosting, models, the bills) go to `get_methods` first: short hand-checked passages (`app/src/agent/methods.ts`). When
those do not answer, `search_tool_docs` (`app/src/agent/docsSearch.ts`) searches the project documents themselves:
README, LIMITS, METHODS, DATA, PLACES, ARCHITECTURE, RULES, CHANGELOG, the two model cards, LICENSES, TALKS, CORPUS,
`shared/ASSUMPTIONS.md` and three sections of HOSTING (the intro, the decision, licences and privacy). Operator pages
(HANDOFF, RUNNING, ADDING_A_CITY) are left out, and so are the district value tables of RULES (the lot tools give those).

chunks.heading: How the assistant answers
chunks.text:
- The index is `app/src/agent/docsIndex.json`, made by `tools/gen_docs_index.ts` and committed. It cuts each document
  by heading into passages of at most about 1,600 characters, text as written, with HTML comments, local paths and
  anything like an email or a key taken out. Each passage has the document, heading path, anchor
  (`docs/LIMITS.md#what-does-not-work-yet`) and a date when its heading or text states one.
- The tool loads the index on first use with a JSON import, the same way `ruleText.ts` loads rule files: a lazy chunk
  in the browser (the main bundle does not grow) and a plain JSON import in Node (eval, tests).
- Ranking: BM25 on the text plus BM25 on the heading path (weight 1.5), a bonus for two of the user's words side by
  side, a light stemmer, project synonyms (ADU, cottage and granny flat; HB 2186 and state bill; Test Site; ParcelIQ
  and Ask; accuracy and mIoU; and more), and a month and day in the question matched to the ISO dates of the
  documents. History and talk notes weigh less unless the question asks about a past day or edit. Up to 4 passages come back with a rule:
  answer only from them, cite the document and heading, and say the documents do not cover it when none matches.
- After any edit to a listed document, regenerate the index: `node_modules/.bin/jiti tools/gen_docs_index.ts`
  (`--check` only reports). `app/src/agent/docsSearch.test.ts` fails when the committed index is stale.

chunks.heading: How the assistant answers
chunks.text:
Eval files: `questions.json` (generated, two cities), `questions_tierb.json`, `questions_ladder.json`,
`questions_allentown.json` and `questions_rule_text.json` (both from `agent/eval/make_more_questions.ts`), and
`questions_features.json` (from `agent/eval/make_feature_questions.ts`). 119 questions in all. The scorer
checks that quoted spans are in a tool result; words the user asked or the assistant searched for are matched word by
word with plurals folded.

Some exceptions read other paths:

- `pipeline/vision/data.py` reads its NAIP images and labels from the course checkout (`ADU_VISION_SOURCE`, default (a local folder)).

chunks.heading: Coordinates
chunks.text: All lengths and areas are computed in a local state plane in feet: EPSG:2272 (NAD83 Pennsylvania South, US feet) for both cities. It is set as `WORK_CRS` in `pipeline/places/philadelphia.py` and `pipeline/places/pittsburgh.py`. Pittsburgh was built in EPSG:2271 (the North zone) before Nov 11, 2026. The current Pittsburgh lot files (data version `pittsburgh-20261114-7ae3f25d22`) record `crs_local` 2272. Erie County (since Nov 27, 2026) is built in EPSG:2271, since Erie lies north of the South zone's band; the lot schema accepts 2271 and 2272. Lot records store geometry as GeoJSON in WGS84 for the map, and name the local system in `lot.crs_local`.

chunks.heading: Ids
chunks.text: A lot id is the county FIPS code, a dash, and the county parcel id. Philadelphia uses the 9 digit OPA account (`42101-051151530`). Pittsburgh uses the county parcel id (`42003-0001D00128000000`). Ids never clash across places.

chunks.heading: Safe writes
chunks.text: Tables that other jobs may read are written under a temporary name, the old file is kept as `<name>.prev.parquet`, and one rename swaps them. A stopped run never leaves half a file. The lot builder records each finished tract in `progress.jsonl` and skips it on the next run.

chunks.heading: Rules
chunks.text:
What the rule files in `shared/rules/` say today for the two lot-level cities and the bills, in plain words. The 223 town files (as of 2026-11-27) are summarized in [RULES_TOWNS.md](RULES_TOWNS.md) (generated by `tools/gen_rules.py towns`). The statewide baseline is described at the end of this page. The tables below were generated by reading the JSON files on 2026-11-11 with a small script. They are not written from memory. To refresh them, read the JSON again. Each line gives the code section and the date the value was last checked against the source ("checked on").

**Not legal advice. Not a zoning determination. Parcel lines are not a survey.** Always confirm with the city or township before you design or build.

chunks.heading: How to read this page
chunks.text:
- "Confidence" is `verified` (read in the primary text), `secondary` (read in an official guide, or a reading of the text that needs care) or `unverified` (not confirmed).
- "not confirmed" means the file holds no value for this rule. The resolver then takes the value from `default.json`, if it has one, and lists the rule as assumed.
- "none set" means the source sets no limit. For example, Pittsburgh has no share-of-house limit.
- A cell marked "(s)" in a district table is `secondary`.
- For bills, "Effect" says how the value applies: it replaces the town value, or it is a floor ("town may not go under") or a cap ("town may not go over").

chunks.heading: Three scenarios
chunks.text:
| Scenario | Philadelphia | Pittsburgh |
|---|---|---|
| Today | `philadelphia` | `pittsburgh` |
| Local reform | `philadelphia` + `bill250042` | same as today (no local bill on file) |
| State reform | `philadelphia` + `hb2186` | `pittsburgh` + `hb2186` |

Bills are not law. Bill 250042 is in committee. HB 2186 passed the House and is in a Senate committee. The state session ends Nov 30, 2026.

`default.json` fills any rule the place leaves unconfirmed, in every scenario. `sb1346.json` is on file but is not applied to either city or in any scenario. The assistant can quote it. Its own file says it does not reach Philadelphia or Pittsburgh. [METHODS.md](METHODS.md) explains the order of work.

chunks.heading: Philadelphia today
chunks.text:
- Instrument: Philadelphia Zoning Code, Title 14, 14-604(11) Accessory Dwelling Units, with 14-604(1) and 14-701
- Status: in force. 14-604(11) as amended by Bills 190612, 210075 and 210078-A. American Legal 2026 code. L&I checklist PZ_004 Rev 3.2022.
- Effective date: none recorded
- File checked on: 2026-11-10
- Checks the tool cannot test from data, shown to the user:
  - Owner must live in the house or the ADU and record an affidavit and deed restriction before final occupancy (14-604(11)(e))
  - Only one street-facing entrance unless a second already existed (14-604(11)(h))
  - ADU must be inside the house or inside a detached accessory building that existed when the 2012 Zoning Code took effect (14-604(11)(c))
  - The district must not otherwise permit more than one dwelling unit (14-604(11)(d)(.2)(.b))
  - Historic properties also need Historical Commission review (14-604(1)(f))
- Notes: The code limits ADUs by overlay, not by council district. Seven overlays carry ADU text (see eligibility.overlay_bars). Most follow council district or ward lines, so the tool can place a lot by overlay list, or by council district and ward when the overlay map is missing.

chunks.heading: Philadelphia today > Rules
chunks.text:
- Approval path when the lot qualifies: Allowed when the lot meets 14-604(11). Zoning permit from L&I.
- Path when the lot does not qualify: Checklist says an ADU is not permitted when the tests fail. Relief would be a Zoning Board variance. The variance section itself was not read.
- House types: Single-family use in a detached or semi-detached building. Attached only in historic structures.
- Only inside an existing building: Inside the principal building or inside a detached accessory building, such as a garage, existing when the 2012 Zoning Code took effect.
- Historic path skips the district, type and lot size tests: Designated or contributing historic buildings qualify in any district and in attached buildings, with no lot size test. The use must still be single-family.
- ADU forms allowed: Interior of the house or of an existing detached accessory building. No new structure.
- Maximum share of the house: No share-of-house limit in the section.
- Minimum size (sq ft): No minimum in the section.
- Historic building may exceed the size cap: Historic structures may exceed 800 sq ft.
- Maximum height of an ADU building (ft): Every accessory structure for a residential use: max 130 sq ft and 15 ft unless the code says otherwise. Applies to a detached or garage ADU building. An internal ADU follows the district height.
- Maximum size of any accessory structure (sq ft): Applies to every residential accessory structure, so a new detached building could not hold an ADU by right.

chunks.heading: Philadelphia today > What this means for a backyard home
chunks.text:
Read from the rules above and checked with `python -m pipeline.rules resolve` for an RSA-5 detached house (2,000 sq ft lot, 1,400 sq ft house, Council District 2, Ward 30, no alley, with an accessory building):

- A unit inside the house or inside an existing garage is by right, if every test passes. No new detached unit is by right anywhere in the city today.
- A new detached unit, a unit over a garage and an attached addition get "variance". Every residential accessory structure is capped at 130 sq ft and 15 ft (14-604(1)(d)), and the ADU must use an existing building (14-604(11)(c)).
- The size cap is 800 sq ft. The owner must live on site. One ADU per lot.
- A unit inside the house uses the district height (38 ft in RSA-5). A garage unit uses the 15 ft accessory cap.
- The rear setback on an alley (5 ft) and the separation from the house (10 ft) came from `default.json` and are listed as assumed.

Across the whole city, 5,469 of the 459,998 lots (1.2 percent) have any legal ADU path today. See [METHODS.md](METHODS.md) section 7.

chunks.heading: Philadelphia today > Overlays
chunks.text:
The overlay check on the built lots found the drawn /SIX overlay and Council District 6 hold the same lots, and the drawn /NE and /FNE overlays and Wards 56, 58, 63 and 66 hold the same lots (see [DATA.md](DATA.md)).

The historic path: a building designated under Chapter 14-1000, or in a historic district and rated contributing by the Historical Commission, may hold an ADU in any district, in an attached building, with no lot size test and no 800 sq ft cap (14-604(11)(c), (d)(.1), (i)). Being inside a district is not enough. The lot data has no contributing rating, so a lot only inside a district does not get the historic path and the record says to confirm with the Commission.

chunks.heading: Pittsburgh today > Administrator's Exception
chunks.text:
The file sets the base path to by right and a separate path for a new detached unit in a side or rear yard: Administrator's Exception (925.06.G.1(i), G.2 and G.3, as amended by Bill 2025-1545 Section 47, confidence `secondary`). The resolver applies it like this:

| ADU type | Path today |
|---|---|
| Inside the house | by right |
| Attached addition | by right |
| Garage conversion | by right |
| New detached unit | Administrator's Exception |
| Unit over a garage, rear lot line on a way and an accessory building on the lot | by right |
| Unit over a garage, otherwise | Administrator's Exception |

The resolver counts an Administrator's Exception as a legal path (as it does a special exception), so a lot where only a detached unit fits still shows as allowed. The stats file carries a caveat that the detached shares are not by-right shares.

Across the whole city all 92,081 lots have a legal ADU path today and none has a new detached unit by right ((a local folder), data version `pittsburgh-20261111-bdeb5697ae`, `all.paths.today`). Pittsburgh has no local bill on file, so local reform equals today.

Notes from the file:

chunks.heading: State reform: House Bill 2186
chunks.text:
- Approval path when the lot qualifies: One ADU per lot or parcel, by right, where a residential building is a permitted use.
- Path for a new detached unit in a side or rear yard: Reading: by right per lot, and a town may not require more than 4 ft from side and rear lot lines, so a local exception for side or rear yards would not hold past 4 ft.
- Zoning districts: Every district where a residential building is permitted.
- House types: Any residential building.
- Minimum lot size (sq ft): No lot size test in the bill. By right per lot or parcel.
- ADU forms allowed: Attached, within, or detached on the same lot. Includes units in a detached garage.
- Maximum size (sq ft): Town max may not be under 50% of the house or 850 sq ft, whichever is less, or a whole basement or attic floor.
- Minimum size (sq ft): Town minimum may not be more than 200 sq ft.
- Maximum height of an ADU building (ft): Town limit may not be under 25 ft or the main house height, whichever is less.
- Side setback (ft): No more than 4 ft for a new structure. None for a conversion of an existing structure.
- Rear setback on an alley or way (ft): The rear lot line cap applies on an alley too.
- ADUs per lot: At least one per lot. A town may allow more.
- Town may bar a separate sale: A town may prohibit separate sale or conveyance. It is a town option, not a ban. Separate rental must be allowed.
- Parking spaces required: No additional off-street parking. Lost garage spaces need not be replaced.

chunks.heading: State reform: House Bill 2186
chunks.text:
How the floors and caps work for one lot: a floor ("town may not go under") raises the town value to the floor when the town value is lower. A cap ("town may not go over") lowers it. The size floor is the lesser of half the house and 850 sq ft, and the height floor is the lesser of 25 ft and the house height, so both need the house size or height. When that fact is missing, the town value stays and a reason says so. Where the town sets no limit at all, a floor or cap does not add one.

Example from the resolver, Philadelphia RSA-5 detached, 1,400 sq ft house, 30 ft tall: every ADU type becomes by right, side and rear setbacks drop to 4 ft, the size floor for this lot is 700 sq ft (so the town's 800 sq ft cap stays), the detached height limit rises to 25 ft and owner occupancy ends.

- **Town files.** As of 2026-11-27, 223 towns beyond the two cities have a cited rule file (`pa_<county>_<town>.json`), mostly the largest by 2020 population. - The rules engine has four new ways to say a town's rule (pass 30, `shared/rules/TOWNS.md`): `employee_quarters` (quarters for the household's employees or caretakers, not an ADU for the public), `status_dispute` (two readings of the code, or a use table against its text: both are cited, the answer says to ask the zoning officer, and counts use the more limiting one), `status_only_if` (a status that holds only for a lot fact, such as a conservation subdivision developed under Option 3) and `status_by_overlay` (a status inside an overlay). Bethel, O'Hara and Penn (Westmoreland) are now verified with them, and Warwick (Lancaster) reads its Village Overlay. Worcester stays drafted: several of its districts were not read. No lot answer moved (regression set: 0 of 50).

chunks.heading: What it is
chunks.text:
An object detector that draws boxes around detached garages, sheds, other accessory buildings and pools in aerial chips of Pittsburgh and Philadelphia. Code: `musa6950/yolo/`. Run: `models/yolo/runs/real/`. Model version tag in its output: `real-d81050e7e0`.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Ultralytics YOLO11 small (`yolo11s.pt` base weights) |
| Input | 640 px chips at 0.5 ft per pixel (320 ft on a side), RGB, leaf off |
| Classes | `garage`, `shed`, `other_accessory`, `pool` |
| Output | `processed/yolo/detections_<city>.parquet`: one row per detected object per lot, with class, score, box in map feet, box area, share in the lot, imagery date and model version |
| License | AGPL-3.0, kept inside `musa6950/yolo/`. Only the detections file leaves the folder |

chunks.heading: Intended use
chunks.text:
- Flag likely detached garages and other accessory buildings that building outline layers miss, so the fit test can treat them as blocks or as garage conversion candidates.
- A first pass for hand review in LabelMe.

**Its detections are not in the lot records.** `pipeline/build_lots.py` writes an empty `objects` list for every lot. Garages and sheds in the lot tool come from building footprints instead: an accessory building of 180 sq ft or more is a garage, a smaller one is a shed. The detections file is read in one place only, the hand-label scoring (`pipeline/validation/score.py`), to compare against hand labels once they exist.

chunks.heading: Training data
chunks.text:
- Imagery: PEMA Orthoimagery Cycle 2. Pittsburgh: West mosaic, flown 2022-03-16 to 2022-04-12. Philadelphia: Eastern PA mosaic, flown 2020-12-11 to 2021-03-22.
- 60 sample areas per city, 9 chips each, 540 chips per city. Areas split 70, 15 and 15 percent, so no area is in two splits.
- **Labels are first pass.** They come from building footprints and OpenStreetMap, not from looking at the image:
  - every footprint on a residential lot that is not the main building is one object
  - `shed` under 180 sq ft
  - `garage` 180 to 700 sq ft and within 75 ft of a street, alley or service lane
  - `other_accessory` everything else
  - `pool` from OpenStreetMap `leisure=swimming_pool`

| City | Split | Chips | Garage | Shed | Other accessory | Pool |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pittsburgh | train | 378 | 558 | 40 | 168 | 3 |
| Pittsburgh | val | 81 | 60 | 7 | 52 | 0 |
| Pittsburgh | test | 81 | 88 | 10 | 79 | 0 |
| Philadelphia | train | 378 | 279 | 37 | 193 | 34 |
| Philadelphia | val | 81 | 78 | 7 | 50 | 25 |
| Philadelphia | test | 81 | 39 | 9 | 51 | 13 |

chunks.heading: Training
chunks.text: 640 px, batch 16, up to 50 epochs with patience 10, seed 6950, Apple MPS. The run stopped after 34 epochs in 26.5 minutes (2026-11-11 06:35 to 07:01).

chunks.heading: Scores
chunks.text:
**The test labels are first-pass labels, not hand checked.** These numbers measure agreement with footprint and OpenStreetMap labels, not true accuracy. A real shed that the footprints miss counts against the model when it finds it.

| Test set | Chips | mAP50 | mAP50-95 | Precision | Recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Both cities | 162 | 0.1692 | 0.0865 | 0.4471 | 0.2237 |
| Pittsburgh | 81 | 0.1934 | 0.0956 | 0.5709 | 0.2601 |
| Philadelphia | 81 | 0.1815 | 0.0934 | 0.4722 | 0.2112 |

AP50 by class:

| Test set | Garage | Shed | Other accessory | Pool |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Both cities | 0.2584 | 0.0331 | 0.2197 | 0.1656 |
| Pittsburgh | 0.3337 | 0.0466 | 0.2001 | no pool labels |
| Philadelphia | 0.16 | 0.026 | 0.2748 | 0.2653 |

At a score threshold of 0.25 (both cities), the model predicted only the garage class: 23 boxes on labeled garages, 25 on labeled other accessory buildings and 12 on background. It missed 104 of 127 labeled garages, all 19 sheds, 105 of 130 other accessory buildings and all 13 pools.

Detections written:

| City | Detections | Lots with a detection | By class |
|---|---|---|---|
| Philadelphia | 198 | 196 | garage 193, pool 5 |
| Pittsburgh | 300 | 292 | garage 297, other accessory 3 |

These cover the sample area chips only, not whole cities.

chunks.heading: Scores > Later runs (Nov 12 to 14)
chunks.text:
Final for the Nov 12 to 14 rounds. Same 162 test chips and the same unchecked labels. Target garage AP50 0.50.

| Run | What changes | mAP50 | Garage | Shed | Other accessory | Pool | Garage, size rule classes (Pittsburgh / Philadelphia) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `real` | the run above | 0.1692 | 0.2584 | 0.0331 | 0.2197 | 0.1656 | |
| `long640` | 80 epochs, cosine schedule | 0.2868 | 0.4062 | 0.0894 | 0.369 | 0.2828 | **0.469** (0.5042 / 0.4093) |
| `pseudo1` | `long640` plus 141 pseudo boxes on train | 0.2644 | 0.401 | 0.0489 | 0.4113 | 0.1966 | 0.4057 (0.5315 / 0.1732) |
| `px960` | 960 px, 40 epochs | 0.1428 | 0.257 | 0.0318 | 0.272 | 0.0102 | |

- Size rule classes: each detected building is classed by the same size and street-distance rule that made the labels, with a box size factor picked on train chips (0.6). With them other accessory rises to 0.4346 and shed falls to 0.0149.
- A run with one building class and the rule after it (`acc2`) was not better (test garage 0.3657).
- Best garage AP50 is 0.469. The 0.50 target is missed overall. Pittsburgh alone passes (0.504).
- Detections in the lot records: still none.

chunks.heading: Limits
chunks.text:
- Labels and images are from different years. Some buildings were built or torn down in between.
- Pittsburgh county outlines skip most small structures, and Philadelphia outlines miss many sheds. A chip with no shed label can still have sheds.
- Garage versus other accessory is a guess from size and distance to an access line.
- OpenStreetMap pools are sparse and mostly public or club pools.
- Accessory buildings on lots that are not residential are not labeled.
- Chips do not overlap, so an object on a chip edge can give two partial detections.
- Pittsburgh chips are in EPSG:2271 (`musa6950/yolo/config.py`), while the Pittsburgh lot build uses EPSG:2272. `detect_lots.py` reprojects the boxes to the lot layer's CRS before the join, so the detections file is consistent. The chip world files stay in EPSG:2271.

chunks.heading: What not to use it for
chunks.text:
- Do not use the scores above as accuracy. They are not, until the test chips are checked by hand.
- Do not count sheds with it. Shed AP50 is 0.0331 (0.0894 in `long640`).
- Do not use a detection as proof that a garage exists, or that it is legal, or what year it was built.
- Do not run it on whole cities and publish the counts as a census of garages.
- Do not import it from product code. Read only the detections file.

chunks.heading: Next step
chunks.text: A review pack of 150 chips per city is ready for hand checking (`musa6950/yolo/REVIEW.md`). The 162 test chips come first. After review, `labelme_to_yolo.py --write` folds the fixes back, and the model is trained and scored again.

chunks.heading: What it is
chunks.text:
A U-Net that labels each pixel of a 4-band aerial image (red, green, blue, near infrared) as land cover. Code: `pipeline/vision/`. Runs: `<data root>/models/<run>/`.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Architecture | U-Net with an ImageNet pretrained ResNet-34 encoder (`segmentation_models_pytorch`), first layer changed to 4 bands |
| Input | NAIP 2022, 0.6 m pixels, 4 bands |
| Output, 4-class runs | other, building, tree, open ground |
| Output, 5-class run | other, building, tree, open ground, hard surface (roads and paving split out of "other") |
| Best 4-class run by test mIoU | `r34ndvi_c4_s1` (NDVI as a fifth input band), 0.7005 |
| Run used for Pittsburgh lot cover | Since 2026-11-18 the three-model ensemble below (`model:div7_3m_tta`), with "other" split into water and hard surface by `r34_c5_s0`. Before that `r34_c5_s0` (5 classes), zero-shot on the city |
| Reference run | `unet_v2_r34`, the earlier published model, scored again: 0.6985 |
| Best result (Nov 18) | Ensemble of `dlv3lov_c4_s1` (DeepLabV3+), `effb2lov_c4_s1` (U-Net with EfficientNet-B2) and `r34c512lov_c4_s1` (U-Net with ResNet-34, 512 px crops), 8 views each, picked on validation. Test mIoU 0.7093, building IoU 0.6554. It passes the Pittsburgh adoption bar, and the Pittsburgh lots use it since 2026-11-18 (see "Later runs") |

chunks.heading: What it is used for in the product
chunks.text:
- Lot records carry a `cover` block: building, tree, open ground and hard surface in sq ft and percent, plus impervious share, source and date. It also gives what lies inside the suggested spot (`spot_cover`), so the tool can say how much canopy a unit would remove.
- In Pittsburgh the source is the three-model ensemble from 2026-11-18 (DeepLabV3+, EfficientNet-B2 and a 512 px ResNet-34, 8 views each), on NAIP 2022 (`model:div7_3m_tta`). Its `spot_cover` comes from the ensemble's class maps (`processed/pittsburgh/cover_work/div7_3m_tta/tiles/`).
- In Allentown and the first 9 county-place towns (lot data 12) the source is `r34_c5_s0` (`model:r34_c5_s0`, NAIP 2022). Their `spot_cover` comes from the same model's class maps (`processed/<place>/cover_work/r34_c5_s0/tiles/`), so it has the same accuracy as the lot shares. The four town places have it since the Nov 15 rebuild. The lots added on Nov 27 and 28 (the 8 new places and the new towns of Chester, Montgomery and Centre) have an empty cover block: the model has not been run on them yet (as of 2026-11-28).
- In Philadelphia the source is **not** this model. It is the city's 2018 land cover raster (`landcover_2018`). See "Transfer to the two cities" below for why.
- Land cover is context only. The fit test is a vector test on lot, building and street data. It does not steer around trees.

chunks.heading: Training data
chunks.text:
- 173 boxes of 1 km around tract population centers in the Chesapeake Bay counties of Pennsylvania, split by county: 122 train (27 counties), 24 validation (7 counties), 27 test (Cumberland and Centre).
- Labels: Chesapeake Bay Program land use and land cover, 2024 edition, "2022" epoch, 1 m, put on the 0.6 m grid with nearest neighbour.
- Labeled pixels: 488,290,379 train, 96,124,030 validation, 109,183,195 test.

| Class share, all boxes | other | building | tree | open | hard |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 classes | 0.1436 | 0.058 | 0.3886 | 0.4099 | |
| 5 classes | 0.0191 | 0.058 | 0.3886 | 0.4099 | 0.1244 |

In the 5-class set "other" is water, wetlands without trees, barren and solar fields. Hard surface is Chesapeake codes 20 (roads), 22 (other impervious) and 31 (extractive impervious).

chunks.heading: Training recipe
chunks.text: Random 384 px crops (1 in 3 centered on a building pixel), flips, 90 degree turns, brightness and contrast jitter. Class-weighted cross entropy plus 0.5 times Dice. AdamW, learning rate 0.0005 (0.001 for the plain U-Net), warmup then cosine decay over 16 planned epochs, stopped at epoch 14. Batch 12, 400 steps per epoch. Apple MPS.

chunks.heading: Scores on the held-out counties
chunks.text:
Test set: every labeled pixel of the 27 test boxes. "TTA" = 8 flips and turns averaged, with a tree offset picked on validation. "Single" = one pass. Edge band = mIoU with the 1 pixel band along label edges left out (a secondary score).

| Run | Test mIoU, TTA | Test mIoU, single | Other | Building | Tree | Open | Accuracy | Edge band | Val mIoU | Minutes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unet_v2_r34` (reference) | 0.6985 | not run | 0.6501 | 0.6449 | 0.706 | 0.7929 | 0.8472 | 0.7643 | not in file | not in file |
| `r34_c4_s1` | 0.699 | 0.6939 | 0.6518 | 0.6404 | 0.71 | 0.7936 | 0.848 | 0.7648 | 0.7348 | 51.1 |
| `r34_c4_s2` (second seed) | 0.6987 | 0.6953 | 0.6516 | 0.6356 | 0.7112 | 0.7962 | 0.8489 | 0.7646 | 0.734 | 53.3 |
| `r34ndvi_c4_s1` (NDVI band) | 0.7005 | 0.6952 | 0.6525 | 0.6427 | 0.7114 | 0.7952 | 0.849 | 0.7668 | 0.7339 | 48.8 |
| `r34ce_c4_s1` (no Dice) | 0.6959 | 0.6914 | 0.6487 | 0.6303 | 0.711 | 0.7934 | 0.847 | 0.7612 | 0.7296 | 48.7 |
| `plain_c4_s1` (no pretrained encoder) | 0.683 | 0.6793 | 0.6372 | 0.6091 | 0.6972 | 0.7886 | 0.8405 | 0.7452 | 0.7154 | 94.2 |
| `r34_c4_s1_lowlr` (4 more epochs at a low rate) | 0.6989 | not run | 0.654 | 0.6451 | 0.7048 | 0.7915 | 0.847 | 0.7652 | 0.7366 | 13.9 |
| `r34_c5_s0`, merged to 4 classes | 0.6957 | not run | 0.6469 | 0.638 | 0.7075 | 0.7905 | 0.8455 | 0.7611 | 0.7121 (5 classes) | 54.8 |

The 5-class run scored on its own 5 classes:

chunks.heading: Scores on the held-out counties
chunks.text:
| Run | Test mIoU | Other | Building | Tree | Open | Hard | Edge band |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `r34_c5_s0` | 0.6528 | 0.4714 | 0.638 | 0.7075 | 0.7905 | 0.6567 | 0.7121 |

By area type (test mIoU, TTA):

| Run | Urban | Suburban | Rural | Urban tree IoU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unet_v2_r34` | 0.6438 | 0.7324 | 0.7178 | 0.5893 |
| `r34_c4_s1` | 0.6428 | 0.7331 | 0.7181 | 0.5895 |
| `r34ndvi_c4_s1` | 0.6443 | 0.7363 | 0.7165 | 0.5894 |
| `plain_c4_s1` | 0.6228 | 0.7171 | 0.7049 | 0.5654 |
| `r34_c5_s0` (5 classes) | 0.6502 | 0.636 | 0.6082 | 0.585 |

Precision and recall for `r34_c4_s1`:

| Class | Precision | Recall |
|---|---|---|
| other | 0.7793 | 0.7994 |
| building | 0.7134 | 0.8623 |
| tree | 0.8331 | 0.8278 |
| open | 0.8995 | 0.8708 |

What the table says:

- Every pretrained ResNet-34 variant lands between 0.6957 and 0.7005 test mIoU. Seeds, NDVI, the loss and extra epochs move the score by less than 0.005.
- The pretrained encoder is the one change that matters: 0.699 against 0.683 for the same recipe without it.
- A test mIoU of 0.72 was not reached by any run in this table. No run here reached a building IoU of 0.65 either. The best here is 0.6451.
- Building recall is higher than precision: the model calls some paving and flat roofs building.

chunks.heading: Scores on the held-out counties > Later runs (Nov 12 to 18)
chunks.text:
Updated Nov 18 with the Nov 17 to 18 night runs. Same test pixels, 8 flips and turns. Ensembles are picked on validation only. 5-class rows are scored as 4 classes here.

| Run or pick | Val mIoU | Test mIoU | Building IoU | Tree IoU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dlv3lov_c4_s1` (DeepLabV3+, Lovasz loss) | 0.7456 | 0.7031 | 0.6507 | 0.7088 |
| `effb2_c4_s1` (EfficientNet-B2 encoder) | 0.7439 | 0.7038 | 0.6441 | 0.717 |
| `effb2lov_c4_s1` (same, Lovasz loss) | 0.7458 | 0.7057 | 0.6506 | 0.7177 |
| 3 ResNet-34 Lovasz models, ensemble | | 0.7035 | 0.6493 | |
| `dlv3lov` + `effb2lov`, 8 views each | 0.7512 | 0.7089 | 0.6546 | 0.7185 |
| 5-class ensemble `effb2lov_c5_s0` + `r34lov_c5_s0`, 8 views | 0.7422 | 0.7009 | 0.6478 | 0.7097 |
| `r34c512lov_c4_s1` (512 px crops, Lovasz loss), 8 views | 0.7464 | 0.705 | 0.6515 | |
| `dlv3c512lov_c4_s1` (DeepLabV3+, 512 px crops, Lovasz loss), 8 views | 0.7464 | 0.7072 | 0.6548 | |
| `dlv3lov` + `effb2lov` + `r34c512lov`, 8 views each (best, picked on validation) | 0.7517 | **0.7093** | **0.6554** | |

chunks.heading: Scores on the held-out counties > Later runs (Nov 12 to 18)
chunks.text:
- Two model types in one ensemble beat more seeds of one type: +0.0054 test mIoU over the ResNet-only ensemble.
- Larger crops (512 px instead of 384) help a little: +0.0023 val and +0.0025 test with Lovasz loss. Adding `r34c512lov_c4_s1` to the ensemble search gave a new best pick on validation (0.7517). It scores 0.7093 on test.
- `dlv3c512lov_c4_s1` ties `r34c512lov_c4_s1` as the best single model on val and is the best single model on test (0.7072). Adding it to the 8-view pick does not raise val, so the best pick keeps three models.
- An EfficientNet-B2 run with 512 px crops ran out of memory headroom on the 18 GB Mac and was not finished.
- Building IoU target 0.65: met (0.6554). mIoU target 0.72: missed (0.7093).
- Adoption for the Pittsburgh lots needs mIoU 0.7136 and building IoU 0.7435 on the clean city pixels (5 classes, "other" split by a 5-class model, water left out). The new three-model ensemble scored 0.7147 and 0.7585, so it passes the bar. One pass of the same three models scored 0.7148 and 0.7622 and passes too. The two-model pair scored 0.7133 and 0.7571 and missed. The 5-class ensemble scored 0.7085 and 0.7524. The Pittsburgh lots use the 8-view ensemble since 2026-11-18. It was picked on validation, so the 8-view pick is used, not the one-pass pick with the higher city score.

chunks.heading: Error analysis
chunks.text:
- Most of the loss is tree against open ground. Open called tree is 24.2 % of wrong pixels and tree called open is 23.1 %.
- The 1 pixel band along label edges is 9.9 % of pixels but 32.3 % of errors. With the band left out mIoU is 0.764.
- Small buildings fail. Building IoU is 0.28 under 50 m2 and 0.50 for 50 to 100 m2.
- The worst label codes are turf grass (26.2 % of errors), other impervious (13.9 %) and tree canopy over turf (13.4 %). Canopy over lawns and paving is where the label (lidar height) and the photo disagree most.
- Moving the prediction by 1 to 2 pixels raises mIoU from 0.699 to 0.708, so label and image are off by about a pixel in places.
- Conclusion: the labels are the limit. Longer training on the same labels is unlikely to reach 0.72.

chunks.heading: Transfer to the two cities
chunks.text: City labels: 2 ft land cover rasters from the University of Vermont Spatial Analysis Lab, 7 classes, grouped to the same 5 classes. Here "other" is water. Philadelphia: 2018 raster, 40 boxes (22 train, 6 val, 12 test). Pittsburgh: 2019 raster, 40 boxes (25 train, 6 val, 9 test). Each city has a zero-shot score (`r34_c5_s0`, no city training) and a fine-tuned run (`ft_c5_<city>`, started from `r34_c5_s0`).

chunks.heading: Transfer to the two cities > Overlap leak in Pittsburgh, corrected
chunks.text:
In Pittsburgh 34.8 % of the test box area was also inside train or validation boxes. The box centers were less than 600 m apart. A first fine-tune score of 0.719 (4 land classes) was inflated by this overlap and is withdrawn. Clean scoring leaves out every test pixel that falls in a train or validation box: 4,839,728 of 7,122,645 test pixels remain. Philadelphia boxes did not overlap.

| Pittsburgh, clean test pixels | mIoU, 5 classes | mIoU without water | As 4 classes | Building | Tree | Open | Hard | Water |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `r34_c5_s0`, zero-shot | 0.703 | 0.7036 | 0.7039 | 0.7335 | 0.8116 | 0.5595 | 0.7097 | 0.7007 |
| `ft_c5_pittsburgh`, fine-tuned | 0.5553 | 0.6941 | 0.6875 | 0.686 | 0.8203 | 0.5619 | 0.7083 | 0.0 |
| `ft_c5_pittsburgh`, overlapping pixels kept (withdrawn) | 0.5755 | 0.7194 | 0.7146 | 0.7288 | 0.8393 | 0.5806 | 0.729 | 0.0 |

- The original model works in Pittsburgh: about 0.70 on clean pixels.
- The fine-tune did not help. It is lower without water (0.6941 against 0.7036), and it lost the water class (IoU 0.0). Lot cover uses the zero-shot model.

chunks.heading: Transfer to the two cities > Philadelphia: a negative result
chunks.text:
| Philadelphia test (12 boxes) | mIoU, 5 classes | As 4 classes | Building | Tree | Open | Hard |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `r34_c5_s0`, zero-shot | 0.3838 | 0.4798 | 0.7072 | 0.2622 | 0.272 | 0.6775 |
| `ft_c5_philadelphia`, fine-tuned | 0.4078 | 0.5097 | 0.7386 | 0.2606 | 0.3226 | 0.717 |
| `unet_v2_r34` (4 classes) | | 0.4777 | 0.7034 | 0.2608 | 0.2686 | |

Tree IoU is about 0.26 with or without city training. The diagnosis found no bug in the class mapping, the alignment or the footprint burn-in. The causes it found:

- NAIP 2022 over Philadelphia was flown 2022-04-30, 05-10 and 05-17, early in the leaf season. The 2018 raster was made from leaf-on 2017 NAIP and 2018 lidar.
- Rowhouse back yards are narrow strips in deep shadow. The label marks many as grass or small trees. The photo shows dark pavement and shadow.
- A simple NDVI threshold reaches only 0.485 vegetation IoU on test, so the photos themselves carry little green.

Decision: Philadelphia lot cover uses the city's 2018 raster. The model output is kept as `cover_model.parquet` for comparison.

chunks.heading: Transfer to the two cities > Per-lot agreement with the city rasters
chunks.text:
| Place, model against raster | Lots compared | Tree MAE (r) | Open MAE (r) | Vegetation MAE (r) | Building MAE (r) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pittsburgh, `r34_c5_s0` against 2019 raster (lot model until Nov 18) | 128 | 8.41 (0.862) | 11.02 (0.844) | 8.16 (0.884) | 7.32 (0.86) |
| Pittsburgh, three-model ensemble against 2019 raster (lot model since Nov 18) | 128 | 8.1 (0.863) | 12.81 (0.841) | 9.48 (0.878) | 6.98 (0.859) |
| Philadelphia, `ft_c5_philadelphia` against 2018 raster | 430,161 | 6.71 (0.622) | 12.02 (0.626) | 13.65 (0.76) | 17.66 (0.805) |

- Pittsburgh has only 128 lots in this check. The 2019 raster covers part of the city, and 801 lots inside the train and val boxes were left out. Treat it as a small check, not a city-wide measure.
- In Pittsburgh `r34_c5_s0` reads tree 6.1 points low on average (12.5 % against 18.6 %). The ensemble reads it 5.4 points low (13.2 %). It is closer on tree and building, but further off on open ground (36.3 % against 25.1 %) and vegetation. On 128 lots these gaps are small either way.
- In Philadelphia the model reads vegetation 11.5 points low (20.2 % against 31.7 %), and worse on rowhouse lots.

chunks.heading: Limits
chunks.text:
- Single models cluster near 0.70 test mIoU on the Chesapeake labels. The best ensemble reaches 0.709. The labels set the ceiling.
- Allentown and the first 9 county-place towns use `r34_c5_s0` per lot. The lots added on Nov 27 and 28 have no cover yet. Only Centre County is a Chesapeake test county (about 0.70 test mIoU). Allentown, Chester and Montgomery are not validated.
- Urban areas score lowest. Urban tree IoU is about 0.59.
- 0.6 m pixels: a small shed is a few pixels and a narrow side yard is a handful.
- Tree canopy over paving is labeled tree. The model cannot see a patio under a tree.
- Philadelphia tree and open ground from NAIP 2022 are not reliable.
- Pittsburgh per-lot agreement rests on 128 lots.
- No hand-labeled lot has been checked against the land cover. See [METHODS.md](METHODS.md) for the hand-label design.

chunks.heading: What not to use it for
chunks.text:
- Do not measure a single building, shed or yard to the square foot.
- Do not use it as a survey, a tree inventory or an impervious surface count for a permit or a fee.
- Do not use it for tree or open ground in Philadelphia.
- Do not use it outside Pennsylvania, or on imagery other than NAIP 4-band, without testing first.

chunks.heading: Models > The AGPL boundary
chunks.text:
- Ultralytics YOLO is AGPL-3.0. It is used only inside `musa6950/yolo/`, with its own `requirements.txt`.
- Nothing outside that folder imports `ultralytics` or any module in it.
- The only thing that leaves the folder is data: `detections_<city>.parquet`.
- `detector.py` is the seam. Another detector under another license can replace YOLO without touching the product.
- The model steps run in a separate Python environment (`geoai`) from the rest of the pipeline (`geospatial`).

Speaking notes for the MUSA 6950 talk. The MUSA 5500 talk notes moved to https://github.com/yezhanggg/YZMUSA5500 (docs/TALKS.md). They are notes, not slides. Each number has its source file in a comment.

chunks.heading: MUSA 6950: remote sensing and deep learning (about 10 minutes) > 1. The question (1 min)
chunks.text:
- Can a backyard home fit on this lot, and what is on the lot now?
- Aerial images give land cover: buildings, trees, open ground, hard surface. Lot, building and street data give the geometry.
- The tool answers for every 1 to 4 unit lot in 14 lot places: Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Allentown, Erie, and towns in ten more counties (1,134,553 lots, Nov 28, 2026).

chunks.heading: MUSA 6950: remote sensing and deep learning (about 10 minutes) > 2. Data and labels (1.5 min)
chunks.text:
- Images: NAIP 2022, 4 bands (red, green, blue, near infrared), 0.6 m pixels.
- Labels: Chesapeake Bay Program land use and land cover, 2024 edition, 1 m. The codes are grouped into 4 classes (other, building, tree, open ground). A 5-class version splits out hard surface.
- 173 boxes of 1 km, split by county: 122 train, 24 validation, 27 test. The test counties are Cumberland and Centre, never seen in training.
- Figures: `musa6950/docs/figures/01_class_shares.png`, `01_image_vs_label.png`.

chunks.heading: MUSA 6950: remote sensing and deep learning (about 10 minutes) > 3. The model comparison (2 min)
chunks.text:
All runs are scored on the same 109,183,195 test pixels, with 8 flips and turns averaged.

| Run | What changes | Test mIoU | Building IoU | Tree IoU | Urban mIoU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Random Forest | pixel features, no context | 0.3602 | | | |
| `plain_c4_s1` | U-Net, no pretrained encoder | 0.683 | 0.6091 | 0.6972 | 0.6228 |
| `r34_c4_s1` | ResNet-34 pretrained, seed 1 | 0.699 | 0.6404 | 0.71 | 0.6428 |
| `r34_c4_s2` | same, seed 2 | 0.6987 | 0.6356 | 0.7112 | 0.6409 |
| `r34ndvi_c4_s1` | adds NDVI as a band | 0.7005 | 0.6427 | 0.7114 | 0.6443 |
| `r34ce_c4_s1` | no Dice loss | 0.6959 | 0.6303 | 0.711 | 0.6387 |
| `r34_c4_s1_lowlr` | extra low learning rate pass | 0.6989 | 0.6451 | 0.7048 | 0.6481 |
| `unet_v2_r34` | the published reference, scored again | 0.6985 | 0.6449 | 0.706 | 0.6438 |
| `r34_c5_s0` | 5 classes (0.6957 when merged to 4) | 0.6528 | 0.638 | 0.7075 | 0.6502 |

- Say plainly: every pretrained single U-Net lands near 0.70.
- The pretrained encoder is the one change that matters (0.683 to about 0.70).

**Nov 12 to 14 runs (final. Training ended Nov 14 at 17:55.)**

chunks.heading: MUSA 6950: remote sensing and deep learning (about 10 minutes) > 3. The model comparison (2 min)
chunks.text:
| Run | What changes | Test mIoU | Building IoU |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dlv3lov_c4_s1` | DeepLabV3+ with Lovasz loss | 0.7031 | 0.6507 |
| `effb2lov_c4_s1` | U-Net, EfficientNet-B2 encoder, Lovasz loss | 0.7057 | 0.6506 |
| 3 ResNet-34 Lovasz models | ensemble, seeds only | 0.7035 | 0.6493 |
| DeepLabV3+ and EfficientNet-B2 | ensemble, 8 views each, picked on validation | 0.7089 | 0.6546 |
| Adding a 512 px ResNet-34 (Nov 18) | ensemble, 8 views each, picked on validation | **0.7093** | **0.6554** |

- Different model types helped where more seeds did not: +0.0054 test over the ResNet-only ensemble.
- Building IoU target 0.65 met (0.6554). mIoU target 0.72 missed (0.7093).
- Pittsburgh: the three-model ensemble scores 0.7147 against the 0.7136 needed to replace the lot model, so it passes. The lots keep `r34_c5_s0` until the owner decides.
- The 512 px crop runs helped a little. Adding the 512 px ResNet-34 to the ensemble moved the best from 0.7089 to 0.7093.
- Figures: `03_training_curve.png`, `03_unet_confusion.png`, `03_example_prediction.png`.

chunks.heading: MUSA 6950: remote sensing and deep learning (about 10 minutes) > 4. What the error analysis showed (1.5 min)
chunks.text:
- Most of the loss is tree against open ground: 47 % of all wrong pixels.
- Label edges: the 1-pixel band along label edges is 9.9 % of pixels but 32.3 % of errors. Without that band mIoU is 0.764.
- Small buildings fail: building IoU 0.28 under 50 m2.
- Urban is the weak place type: mIoU 0.644 urban, 0.732 suburban, 0.718 rural.
- Canopy over lawn and over pavement is where the label (lidar height) and the photo disagree most.
- Conclusion: the labels are the limit, not the training. More epochs and seeds all land at the same place.
- Figures: `07_error_confusion_size.png`, `07_worst_tiles.png`.

chunks.heading: MUSA 6950: remote sensing and deep learning (about 10 minutes) > 5. Transfer to two cities (1.5 min)
chunks.text:
| City and model | mIoU without water | Tree IoU |
|---|---|---|
| Pittsburgh, original model, clean test pixels | 0.7036 | 0.8116 |
| Pittsburgh, city fine-tune, clean test pixels | 0.6941 | 0.8203 |
| Pittsburgh, city fine-tune, first score (withdrawn) | 0.7194 | 0.8393 |
| Philadelphia, original model (4-class view) | 0.4798 | 0.2622 |
| Philadelphia, city fine-tune (4-class view) | 0.5097 | 0.2606 |

- Pittsburgh: the original model transfers well. The fine-tune did not help, and it lost the water class (water IoU 0.0).
- **The withdrawn score.** 34.8 % of the Pittsburgh test box area sat inside training boxes. The first fine-tune score (0.719) came from that overlap. The split code now keeps boxes apart, and city scores leave out the overlapping pixels.
- **Philadelphia is a negative result.** Tree IoU is about 0.26 with or without fine-tuning.
  - The NAIP 2022 flights over Philadelphia were Apr 30 to May 17, early leaf. Rowhouse back yards sit in deep shadow.
  - Checks found no label bug and no shift.
  - So Philadelphia lots use the city's 2018 land cover raster instead of the model.
- Figure: `08_philadelphia_chips.png`.

chunks.heading: MUSA 6950: remote sensing and deep learning (about 10 minutes) > 6. How the model output feeds the lot tool (1 min)
chunks.text:
- The fit test does not use the land cover. It is a vector geometry test on the lot outline, the buildings and the streets, with setbacks from the rule files. It finds the largest unit that fits and where.
- Land cover adds context to each lot: tree canopy, open ground, hard surface and impervious share. In the six places of lot data 12 it also gives the trees and paving inside the suggested spot (the four town places since Nov 15). The places added on Nov 27 and 28 have no land cover yet.
- Sources: since Nov 18 the Pittsburgh lots use the three-model ensemble (DeepLabV3+, EfficientNet-B2 and a 512 px ResNet-34). Before that they used the original 5-class model. The Philadelphia lots use the 2018 raster. Allentown and the first 9 county-place towns use the 5-class model (added Nov 14). Only Centre County lies in a test county (about 0.70). Allentown, Chester and Montgomery are not validated, and each record says so.
- Per-lot check against the city rasters (tree share):
  - Pittsburgh: the ensemble is off by 8.1 points on average since Nov 18 (the 5-class model by 8.41), but only 128 lots could be checked.
  - Philadelphia: the model is off by 6.71 points on 430,161 lots, which is why it is not used.
- The detector (YOLO, outbuildings), final: garage AP50 0.469 (target 0.50). The first run scored 0.2584. Two changes did it: 80 epochs at 640 px (0.4062), then setting garage, shed or other by the same size and distance rule that made the labels (0.469, with Pittsburgh 0.504 and Philadelphia 0.409). That score is against first-pass labels from footprints, not hand-checked labels, so it is not a true accuracy. Detections are not in the lot records. Garages come from building footprints.

- Figures: `10_detector_pr_curve.png`, `10_detector_confusion.png`, `09_pittsburgh_lot_sheet.png`.
