chunks.heading: MUSA 6950: remote sensing and deep learning (about 10 minutes) > 8. What is not measured yet (30 s)
chunks.text:
- Fit accuracy against a person. 250 lots are sampled, and no person has labeled them. On Nov 26 a vision model labeled them from the aerial photo and the lot outline, following the hand-label protocol (`labels_claude/`). It agrees with the product on 84.2% of Pittsburgh and 84.7% of Philadelphia lots at 600 sq ft. These are not hand labels. `pipeline/validation/protocol_fit.py` scores the product with the protocol's own test (86.5% at 600 sq ft).
- Detector accuracy against checked labels. The labels are still unchecked.
- Land cover for Pittsburgh lots is checked on only 128 lots. In Allentown, Chester and Montgomery it is not checked at all. The lots added on Nov 27 and 28 have no land cover yet.

chunks.heading: MUSA 6950: remote sensing and deep learning (about 10 minutes) > 9. Likely questions
chunks.text:
1. **"Why not train longer or on a bigger model?"** We tried other model types too. Single models land near 0.70. An ensemble of two model types reached 0.709. The error analysis puts a third of the errors on label edges and half on tree against open ground, where the label and the photo disagree. More training on the same labels would not fix that.
2. **"So is the fit answer right?"** We do not know yet. The geometry is exact for the data it gets, but parcel lines and footprints have errors. The hand-label check is set up, with 250 lots, sheets and a scoring script, and no person has labeled them. A vision model labeled them on Nov 26 and agrees on about 84% at 600 sq ft, but that is not a hand label. Until a person labels them the fit has no measured accuracy.
3. **"Why keep a model that failed in Philadelphia?"** It works in Pittsburgh on the photos we have. In Philadelphia the 2022 photos do not show the trees, so we used the better source. Reporting that is part of the result.

---

chunks.heading: Live demo script (about 2 minutes)
chunks.text:
Uses the lot data as it is today. The lot ids below were checked in (a local folder) on 2026-11-12. All five steps are also covered by the browser tests in `app/e2e/lot-flow.spec.ts` (9 passed on 2026-11-12).

1. **A Pittsburgh lot that fits.** Open `#/?view=test&lot=42003-0086N00208000000&tract=42003141300` (5459 Beacon St). The answer reads "Yes, with approval": a 20 x 30 ft cottage fits, through an Administrator's Exception. The checklist shows the 1,000 sq ft size cap; open the "Approval path" row for its section. Drag the unit box to show the fit test follow it, and zoom the site view with + and −.

2. **A Philadelphia rowhouse that is not allowed today.** Search "1818 E Moyamensing Ave" or open `#/?view=test&lot=42101-011000034&tract=42101002702`. The answer reads "No", with the rule's own reason (attached building). Open the "Lot size" row for the section, or the Why fold for every reason.

3. **The scenario switch.** On the same lot, click the "Local Bill" chip (Bill 250042) and then "State Bill" (HB 2186). Each chip carries a "not law" tag. Say again: bills, not law.
4. **The Next Step tab.** Open Next Step: a one-line summary, then up to six plain steps (who, how long, cost, official link), from checking the rules to the rental license; on a "No" lot it says what would have to change. Then the Money fold on Results with cost and rent.
5. **Boundaries.** Turn on Census Tract (one boundary at a time): the tracts are coloured by their ADU rule. Click one for its answer and its towns.

chunks.heading: Machine-read zoning layer: design
chunks.text:
Date: 2026-11-11, tier B added 2026-11-12. Status: the quote search (tier B, below) is in the assistant. The machine drafts are not: no status, path or district from this pipeline reaches the product. Code: `pipeline/corpus/`. Data and outputs: `<data root>/corpus/`.

Not legal advice. Not a zoning determination.

chunks.heading: The idea in one line
chunks.text: Keep the hand-checked rule files as they are. Add a second, clearly weaker layer: the town's own ordinance text, searchable, with a machine draft that quotes it. Fall back to the statewide baseline when neither exists.

chunks.heading: Three tiers, kept apart
chunks.text:
| Tier | What it is | How the assistant may use it | Label shown |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Hand-checked rule file | `shared/rules/pa_*.json` (131 towns: 86 verified, 45 drafted, as of 2026-11-15. As of 2026-11-27: 223 towns, 199 verified and 24 drafted) and the two city files, read and checked against the code | State values, cite section, link and check date | "Checked rule file, verified on <date>" |
| B. Public zoning text | Ordinance text fetched from the town or county site, split into sections | Quote passages word for word with section, pages, link and fetch date. No verdict | "Unverified text search" |
| C. Statewide baseline | `shared/rules/pa_statewide.json` | MPC paths, building code, sewage, bills | "Statewide baseline, not this town's code" |

Order: A wins. B is used for a place with no A file, or for a detail the A file lacks, kept apart and labelled. C is given beside B.

Rules for tier B answers (in the system prompt and the tool result):
- Quote word for word in quotation marks, with section, link and date fetched. Say it is unverified text and to confirm with the town.
- Never turn quotes into a verdict: no allowed / not allowed / by right, no approval path, no district list, unless a quoted sentence says it, attributed to the quote.
- No match: "Not found in the text searched", and only when the full text is on file. With partial text the answer says the text on file is incomplete.
- OCR text is quoted as returned, reading errors included, and said to come from a scan.
- The machine drafts (status, path, districts, "not addressed") are never served. The pilot showed them wrong for 2 of 5 towns, one a false "not addressed".

chunks.heading: Pilot results
chunks.text:
**Set.** 31 places with a public copy of the ordinance were tried. 28 were fetched (3 refused by robots.txt, 1 link gone). 146 files, 141 documents extracted. 54 documents are scans with no text layer, and 7 places have only scans. About a quarter of public copies need OCR. 24 places had usable text: 6,367 chunks.

**Retrieval.** Hit = the section cited in the hand-checked file is in the top k. 44 questions on 5 towns.

| System | Top 5 | Top 10 |
|---|---|---|
| BM25 only | 70% | 80% |
| bge-small vectors | 77% | 86% |
| bge-small hybrid | 80% | 89% |
| e5-base vectors | 84% | 93% |
| e5-base hybrid | 84% | 93% |

On the verified towns only (37 questions, 4 towns) e5 hybrid finds the section in the top 10 for 92%. The fallback path (usually an MPC reading, not a sentence in the code) is found for 33%. One question moves a rate by 2 to 25 points, so these are small samples.

**Extraction.** Claude Haiku 5.5 drafts a summary with quotes, three runs on six scored towns:

| Field | Result |
|---|---|
| ADU status, raw | 4 of 6 |
| ADU status, with the consistency rule | 5 of 6 in two runs, 4 of 6 in one |
| Approval path | 4 of 6 |
| Fallback path | 0 of 4 |
| Districts | mean Jaccard 0.2 to 0.35, exact in 1 of 5 |
| Size caps | 8 of 9 in every run |
| Owner occupancy | 4 of 5 |
| Family-only flag | 1 of 5 |
| Conditions found | 22 of 31 |
| Quotes found verbatim in the cited text | 74 of 75 |

On verified towns only (5 towns): status raw 3 of 5, path 4 of 5, family flag 0 of 4, conditions 15 of 23.

chunks.heading: Pilot results
chunks.text:
**Drafts read by hand.** Five drafts for towns with no hand-checked file were read against the text. 2 were right as shown, 1 partly right (a rule true in four districts read as town-wide) and 2 wrong. One of the wrong ones said "no ADU text found" for a town whose code defines an accessory dwelling and permits it in its district tables. The quote check passed because the quote was real.

**Data problems found.** One place's link led to a county home page, so its draft said "not addressed" from a menu page. Two places share their county's ordinance and had no text. The code was fixed and the text rebuilt. The drafts for those three places were not redone.

**What this means.** Retrieval works well enough to point a reader to the right section. The machine draft is not reliable enough to state a town's rule: it misses conditions, mixes up district lists held in tables, cannot give the fallback path, and can call a town silent when it is not. That is why it stays out of the product, and why tier B answers would quote text rather than state conclusions.

**Cost.** About $0.004 to $0.005 and 7 to 9 s per town for the draft. $0.49 spent in the pilot.

chunks.heading: Tier B in the product (2026-11-12)
chunks.text:
**Build.** `python -m pipeline.corpus.tierb build` writes `<data root>/corpus/tierb/`: `manifest.json` (one row per place: name, county, GEOID, text file, own site or county ordinance, links, date fetched, document date, `complete` with reasons when not, OCR flag, rule file status, how many PA towns share the name) and `text/<id>.json.gz` (documents, then passages as `[doc, section, heading, first page, last page, text]`). No drafts in either. `publish <dir>` copies them. `eval` runs the retrieval check below. No network, no model.

**Places.** 66 places from 29 texts. 26 places have their own text, 8 of them read wholly or partly by OCR from scans (Robesonia, Boggs, Beaver, Middle Paxton, Ridgway, Wilkes-Barre, parts of Mont Alto and Whitehall). 40 places are covered by a county ordinance already fetched: Luzerne (19, list from the county zoning page), Lycoming (19, Zoning Partnership list), Warren (2). The county lists are in `corpus/sources/county_coverage.csv`. 61 places have the full text on file. 5 do not: South Middleton, Mont Alto, Manheim, Whitehall (separate article files), Abington (2017 base text, 16 later amendments not included; `corpus/sources/tierb_overrides.csv`). 7 places also have a rule file.

chunks.heading: Tier B in the product (2026-11-12)
chunks.text:
Every own-site and county source in `availability.csv` (39 rows) was already in the pilot, so no new source could be added from it and nothing was fetched. The rest of the 60-place extension came from mapping county ordinances to the places their county page lists. OCR: tesseract through ocrmypdf, 53 scanned documents, 1,311 pages, about 20 minutes of CPU. Quotes from OCR text are verbatim of the OCR, not of the scan.

**Size.** 15.9 MB of text, 4.3 MB gzipped (median 138 kB, largest 0.28 MB per file). A county ordinance is stored once.

**Search: lexical, no vectors.** BM25 in the browser or Node over one place's passages, with a plural stem and query expansion for ADU words ("ADU" also searches accessory, apartment, in-law, granny, carriage, cottage, secondary) and size, parking, height and owner words at half weight. On the pilot retrieval questions (37, verified towns, cited section in the top k):

| Search | Top 5 | Top 10 |
|---|---|---|
| BM25 as in the pilot | 78% | 81% |
| + plural stem | 84% | 86% |
| + query expansion (shipped) | 84% | 89% |
| e5-base hybrid (pilot, needs a model) | 84% | 92% |

The expansion was tuned on the same questions, so 89% is optimistic. Vectors would need the embedding model in the browser, or a server function that embeds the query; the API route runs no tools. One question of difference does not justify either.

chunks.heading: Tier B in the product (2026-11-12)
chunks.text:
A passage counts as a match when it has most of the question's words, the rarest one included. For an ADU question it must also name an ADU (`ADU_PHRASES`: accessory dwelling, accessory apartment, dwelling for a relative, conversion apartment, separate residential dwelling unit and others), so "accessory" and "dwelling" scattered through a definitions page do not count. No match gives no passages and the not-found wording. Passages longer than 1,400 characters are cut to a contiguous excerpt (always an exact substring) around the ADU name or the query words.

**Tools** (`app/src/agent/zoningText.ts`, in `agent/schema.ts` TOOLS, run by `app/src/agent/executors.ts`):
- `search_zoning_text(place, county?, query, k?)`: `{tier: "B", label, place, query, source: {kind, document_date, fetched_on, full_text_on_file, incomplete_because?, ocr?}, found, results: [{quote, section, heading, pages, url, fetched_on, ocr?, words_matched}], how_to_use, next_step}`, plus `rule_file_first` for a town with a rule file. A shared name with no county (13 Penn townships) returns `ambiguous` and asks for the county.
- `list_text_places(county?)`: the places, completeness, dates and rule file status.
- `get_rule_text` adds `text_search` when a town has no rule file but has text.

chunks.heading: Tier B in the product (2026-11-12)
chunks.text:
**Where the files are read.** Browser: `VITE_ZONING_TEXT_URL`, else the lot data URL with `lots/` replaced by `zoning_text/`, else `/data/zoning_text/`. Node (tests, eval): `ZONING_TEXT_DIR`, default (a local folder). The publishable copy is (a local folder) (4.2 MB), next to `host/lots/`: it goes to the same Pages repository with the lot data (docs/HOSTING.md step 4), so with `VITE_LOT_DATA_URL` set no new setting is needed. The API route (`api/agent.ts`) only passes the tool definitions to the model; tools run in the browser.

**Eval.** `agent/eval/questions_tierb.json`, 10 questions (category `tier_b`), read with the generated set. Checks: every quoted span of 4 words or more is in a passage or tool result of the run; verdict and absence patterns outside quotes; not-found wording only with full text; county ordinance named; shared name asks for the county; a verified town answered from its rule file; a town with no text quotes nothing. Claude Haiku 5.5, last three runs after the fixes: 10, 7 and 10 of 10 (27 of 30). Made-up citations 0. One quote not in the text in 30 answers: the model fixed OCR errors inside a quote. Other misses: "doesn't mention" for a no-match, and asking for the county of a unique name. About $0.02 a run.

chunks.heading: Eval questions planned in the pilot (agent/eval)
chunks.text:
For towns in tier B only, and for the tier A towns that also have own-site text (used as the check):
1. "Can I build an ADU in <town>?" Must call `search_zoning_text`, quote a section, show the machine-read label and the zoning officer line. Fail if it states allowed or not allowed without a quote.
2. "What is the size limit for an ADU in <town>?" Number must appear in a quoted span. Fail on a number with no quote.
3. A town whose summary says `not_addressed` (absence). Must say "not found in the text searched", not "prohibited".
4. A tier A town that also has tier B text. Must answer from tier A and not mix in tier B values.
5. A town with no text at all. Must fall back to the statewide baseline and say so.
6. A district question for a district-only rule (York SE in six districts, not CBD). Must not call the rule town-wide.
7. Family-only towns (Manheim, Abington). The answer must keep the relative condition.
8. A stale source (Wilkes-Barre 2012, Penn Hills 2020). Must give the document date.

chunks.heading: Training a custom model: what it would and would not add
chunks.text:
- There were 133 hand-checked rule files (131 towns and the two cities, 2026-11-15), and 225 as of 2026-11-27 (223 towns and the two cities, 201 verified). That is the test set, not a training set. Training on them would leave nothing honest to measure with.
- A fine-tuned extractor would learn the format of 133 answers, not the law of 2,500 towns. The hard parts are retrieval (finding the use table row and the conditions), reading flattened tables, and keeping conditions and scope. None of these get better from 133 examples.
- Retrieval plus a small general model plus a quote check is cheaper to run, easy to audit (every claim has a span), and does not need labels. The verified towns stay a clean test set.
- What could help later: a small reranker or embedding fine-tune trained on (question, cited section) pairs from the rule files, if the pilot grows to a few hundred checked pairs. Gain would be in retrieval only, and only a few points.

chunks.heading: What the local GPU is for
chunks.text:
- Embeddings. bge-small runs at about 120 chunks/s on MPS against 20 on CPU. e5-base about 43 against 6. All public Pennsylvania text (about 200k chunks) embeds in about 30 minutes with bge-small or about 80 minutes with e5-base on a laptop GPU (Apple MPS).
- Re-embedding after a change, and trying other embedding models or a reranker.
- Possibly OCR for scanned PDFs (a quarter of public copies), if a local OCR model is added later.
- It is not needed for extraction. The extraction call is a hosted model and costs under half a cent per town.

chunks.heading: Money assumptions
chunks.text:
Every number the cost, rent and pay-off model uses lives in one file: `shared/assumptions.json`.
The Python pipeline (`pipeline/money.py`) and the browser (`app/src/lib/money.ts`) both read it.
Nothing else holds a cost, rate or tax number.

This page lists each one: what it is, its value and range, where it comes from and how sure we are.

chunks.heading: How sure we are
chunks.text:
| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| measured | We computed it from an official file (for example the 2026 average of weekly mortgage rates). |
| published | An official or public statistic, fee schedule or law. |
| vendor | A builder, lender, insurer or cost website estimate. No official source exists. |
| assumption | Owner judgement. Change it freely. |

Pennsylvania has no official ADU cost data. All build costs are vendor numbers, so each has a low, mid and high value.
Pages with no date carry the day they were read (2026-11-10).

chunks.heading: What the model does
chunks.text:
1. **Cost.** Build cost = size x cost per sq ft for the type x size curve x area cost factor x finish level.
   Then add site work, utility runs, septic if the lot has no public sewer, contingency (on build, site and utilities),
   design (on build), permit fees, water and sewer tap fees, survey, and the Philadelphia construction tax.
   Each item has a low, mid and high value. Low adds up all the low values. High adds up all the high values.
2. **Rent.** Size gives a bedroom count (studio under 450 sq ft, 1 bedroom under 750, else 2).
   Rent is the HUD Small Area Fair Market Rent for the ZIP and that bedroom count.
   Where a ZIP has no SAFMR, use ACS tract median rent by bedrooms.
3. **Running costs.** Vacancy, a management fee if the owner does not manage it, a maintenance reserve, insurance, the rental license and the added property tax.
4. **Tax.** The assessor adds the build cost (mid) to the value. Philadelphia taxes it at 1.3998 percent, with the 10-year abatement that falls 10 points a year.
   Pittsburgh taxes it at 2012 base-year value (about 49 percent of today's value) times county, city and school millage.
   Elsewhere it uses the state median effective rate.
5. **Loan.** A preset gives loan to cost, rate and term. The rest is paid in cash.
6. **Results.** Monthly cash flow, break-even rent, payback years, yield on cost, cash-on-cash return, debt coverage,
   an added value estimate, and a verdict.

chunks.heading: Verdict rules
chunks.text:
With a loan:

- **pays**: monthly cash flow at the mid cost is 0 or more, and net operating income is at least 1.20 times the loan payment.
- **close**: it does not pay, but it pays at the low cost, or the monthly gap is within 10 percent of rent.
- **does_not_pay**: everything else.

Paid in cash:

- **pays**: yield on cost (yearly net operating income over total cost) is at least the 30-year mortgage rate.
- **close**: the yield is within 10 percent of that rate, or the low-cost yield clears it.
- **does_not_pay**: everything else.

The test uses the average property tax of the first 10 years, so the Philadelphia abatement counts but does not decide the answer alone.
Change `verdict.rules` to use year 1 or full tax.

chunks.heading: What it gives today (600 sq ft, mid cost, all-in per sq ft)
chunks.text:
| Type | Philadelphia | Pittsburgh | Rest of PA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Detached new | 338 (259 to 469) | 314 (240 to 439) | 318 (239 to 448) |
| Attached | 302 (233 to 410) | 279 (216 to 381) | 279 (216 to 381) |
| Over garage | 357 (271 to 484) | 330 (251 to 450) | 334 (250 to 459) |
| Garage conversion | 236 (160 to 353) | 217 (147 to 328) | 221 (146 to 337) |
| Internal conversion | 194 (128 to 292) | 178 (117 to 269) | 178 (117 to 269) |

Smaller units cost more per sq ft. A detached unit in Philadelphia is about 462 per sq ft at 300 sq ft and 272 at 1,000 sq ft (mid).
Rest of PA adds a mid 3,000 sewer tap fee for new services, which is why it is a little above Pittsburgh.

chunks.heading: How to change a number
chunks.text:
1. Edit the item in `shared/assumptions.json`. Keep `low <= mid <= high`. Update `sources` (title, url, date) and `confidence`.
   An owner choice is `"confidence": "assumption"` with the source `Owner setting`.
2. Change `version` at the top to today's date.
3. Rebuild the parity cases: `python -m pipeline.money fixture`.
4. Run the checks:
   - `python -m pytest tests/test_money.py -q`
   - `npx vitest run app/src/lib/money.test.ts`
5. Look at one result: `python -m pipeline.money demo --zip 19143 --size 600 --type detached_new --place philadelphia`.

The browser imports the JSON at build time, so a site rebuild picks up the change.

To refresh rents: `python -m pipeline.market download --force`. HUD updates SAFMRs once a year (fiscal year starts 1 October).
Then change `fiscal_year` in `rents.source`.

To refresh the mortgage rate: read the last row of the Freddie Mac PMMS history file and update `financing.pmms30`, `financing.pmms15` and the date.

chunks.heading: Known gaps
chunks.text:
- No Pennsylvania ADU cost survey. Build costs are vendor numbers calibrated to land near 300 to 360 per sq ft all-in for a small detached unit in Philadelphia.
- The size curve, finish levels, site work and utility costs for types other than detached are judgement.
- Philadelphia: whether an ADU gets the new-construction abatement (phased) or the improvement abatement (flat 100 percent, owner-occupied only) is decided by the Office of Property Assessment. The 1 percent construction tax rate was not verified.
- Pittsburgh: Chapter 267 rental abatement terms were not verified, so no abatement is applied. Zoning review fee not found.
- Rest of PA: permit fees use the Pittsburgh schedule as a stand-in. Tap-in fees vary by sewer authority.
- Insurance is a whole landlord policy. Adding an ADU to the house policy may cost less.
- Added value is an income estimate. A backyard unit does not sell on its own.

chunks.heading: Hosting the lot data
chunks.text:
Testing mode reads per-tract lot files and parcel tiles that are too big for this repository. They are served from
other public GitHub repositories through GitHub Pages. Since Nov 28 the lot data bundle is 1,713.5 MB, split over two repositories of 867.1 MB and 846.4 MB (see below). It costs nothing and needs no new account.

This page has the decision, the steps to publish, how to update the data, and how to roll back.

chunks.heading: Decision
chunks.text:
GitHub Pages from a separate public repository. Fallback: jsDelivr in front of the same repository, split per city.

| Option | Limits (checked Nov 11, 2026) | PMTiles by range | CORS | `.json.gz` | Owner work | What can go wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GitHub Pages, second repo** | Site up to 1 GB. Repo ideally under 1 GB. Soft 100 GB a month bandwidth. Soft 10 builds an hour. 10 minute deploy timeout. Files over 100 MiB blocked | Yes, 206 on GET | `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on files. Not on 404 pages. OPTIONS gets 405, so only simple requests work (the app sends only those) | Sent as `application/gzip`, no `Content-Encoding`. The loader unzips it | Create repo, push, turn on Pages, set one env var | Over 100 GB a month GitHub may ask to move. Repo grows by the changed files on each update. 10 minute cache after an update |
| jsDelivr from the same repo | 150 MB per repo and 20 MB per file by default. Tags cached for a year, branches 12 h. Purge by request | Yes | `*` | Raw bytes | Same repo, plus a tag | 985 MB is over the 150 MB cap, so it needs one repo per city plus a split of Philadelphia, or a request to jsDelivr. Their rules say not a general file host |
| GitHub Releases assets | 2 GiB per file, 1000 files per release | Yes | None. The download redirects to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` with no CORS header | | | The browser cannot fetch them from the app. Ruled out |

chunks.heading: Decision
chunks.text:
| Inside the Vercel deployment | Hobby: 100 GB a month transfer, 45 min build, no stated cap on build output. CLI upload 100 MB on Hobby (a June 2026 changelog says CLI limits were removed, unclear for Hobby) | Yes | Same origin | Can set headers in `vercel.json` | Files must be in the git repo or fetched at build time | 952 MB in the app's git history forever. iCloud syncs the repo folder. Every deploy uploads it again |
| Vercel Blob | Hobby: 1 GB storage, 10 GB a month transfer, 2,000 advanced operations | Yes | Configurable | Raw | Enable Blob in the Vercel project | 10 GB a month is about 7,000 first lot views. Access stops for the rest of the month when a limit is passed |
| Cloudflare R2 | 10 GB storage, free egress, 1 M writes and 10 M reads a month | Yes | Configurable | Raw | New Cloudflare account and billing setup | Needs a new account. Ruled out |

Why Pages:

- It is the only option with no new account, no size split and CORS on by default.
- Range requests work, so the parcel tiles load piece by piece (about 20 to 120 KB per map view).
- The first lot of a tract costs about 1 MB. At 100 GB a month that is about 100,000 first lot views.
- The data lives apart from the app. An app deploy does not upload the 1.7 GB of lot data, and the app repo stays small.

chunks.heading: Decision
chunks.text:
Fallback if Pages stops serving (bandwidth or policy): push the same bundle as two repos (one per city, Philadelphia
split in two) and use jsDelivr URLs pinned to a tag. Or enable Vercel Blob in the project. Only `VITE_LOT_DATA_URL`
changes. Since Nov 27 the app can also read each place from its own base URL (`VITE_LOT_DATA_URLS`, see above), so a split no longer needs one host.

Sources:

- GitHub Pages limits: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits
- Large files on GitHub: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/working-with-files/managing-large-files/about-large-files-on-github
- `.nojekyll`: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/creating-a-github-pages-site
- jsDelivr limits and caching: https://github.com/jsdelivr/jsdelivr (README)
- GitHub Releases: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases
- Vercel limits: https://vercel.com/docs/limits and https://vercel.com/docs/limits/fair-use-guidelines
- Vercel Blob: https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing
- Cloudflare R2: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/
- Headers seen on github.io sites with curl (Nov 11, 2026): `206`, `access-control-allow-origin: *`,
  `cache-control: max-age=600`, `.gz` as `application/gzip` with no `content-encoding`, `.json` gzipped on the fly,
  404 and OPTIONS with no CORS header.

chunks.heading: Licences and privacy
chunks.text:
- The data repo README repeats the licence notes from `docs/LICENSES.md`. Some city and county layers state no
  licence (Allegheny County on PASDA, City of Pittsburgh ArcGIS layers). The City of Philadelphia License allows free
  public use but does not say if copies may be republished. Publishing the derived files is a judgement call. Ask the
  providers if the tool goes beyond a class project.
- Microsoft building outlines and OpenStreetMap are ODbL. The derived records are shared under the ODbL with credit.
- No owner names or mailing addresses are in the files. Each record has the address, year built, living area,
  stories and ZIP code of the parcel, from public assessment records.
- No assessed values and no sale dates or prices. The lot build on the drive keeps `facts.assessed_value`,
  `facts.last_sale_date` and `facts.last_sale_price`, but nothing in the app or the assistant reads them, so
  `tools/publish_lots.sh` leaves them out of every published tract file (the drive files are not changed) and
  checks the bundle for them. The assistant's `get_lot_facts` answers "not in the public data" for them, from a
  published or a local record alike. `tests/test_publish_lots.py` runs the script on a small fake build.
- `tools/publish_lots.sh` removes the build machine's folder paths from `manifest.json` and from the PMTiles metadata.
- The tile files carry only lot ids, the tract, the housing form, today's largest cottage size and the packed answers
  (`id`, `tr`, `s`, `t`, `mf`, `mk`, `a`; the overview `a`, `n`, `d`). `tools/publish_lots.sh` stops if a tile file
  lists any other property.
- Not legal advice. Not a survey.
